# Native tool-error transcript experiment

Read-only protocol note (2026-09-24). No app/source/build/model work was performed for this note.

The current correction request already puts `rejectedProposal` and `validationFeedback` in the capture function's `role=tool` result. This is not a move from user message to tool message. The proposed representation change removes those two fields from the capture result, then replays the rejected answer as an assistant function call followed by a host-generated matching `role=tool` validation-error result. Keep the original capture result and trusted user goal unchanged. No hidden reasoning is replayed.

At pinned llama.cpp commit [`6eddde06a4f25d55d538b5d15628dcc2b6882147`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/6eddde06a4f25d55d538b5d15628dcc2b6882147), Qwen3.5's template serializes assistant tool calls at physical lines 105–130 and wraps `role=tool` contents as `<tool_response>` at lines 131–142. It starts the next assistant generation with a `<think>` prefix at lines 147–154. The raw template has 154 physical lines, so earlier rendered-page line numbers are invalid. The pinned server README documents tool calls with `--jinja` at physical lines 1310–1314: [README lines 1310–1314](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/6eddde06a4f25d55d538b5d15628dcc2b6882147/tools/server/README.md#L1310-L1314). See the verified [Qwen3.5 template lines 105–154](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/6eddde06a4f25d55d538b5d15628dcc2b6882147/models/templates/Qwen3.5-4B.jinja#L105-L154).

The standard function-call flow also retains the assistant call and supplies its result keyed by call ID before requesting the next model turn; see the [official function-calling flow](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#how-it-works) and [Chat Completions example](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#handling-function-calls). These sources establish a supported message shape, not that the local model will correct more reliably.

A bounded experiment can compare the existing four-role inline-feedback request with a six-role request containing the same capture, then the exact rejected assistant answer call and matching host validation-error result. Hold system/user instructions, tool schemas, request settings, model, capture, token profile, correction count, and host validation constant. Record prompt token count and whether the single permitted correction fixes the concrete missing-evidence case. Keep the host validator authoritative; do not relax evidence/reference checks or add retries. A structurally valid tool call alone is not evidence of progress or model quality.

The prepared diagnostic was statically inspected (not executed): its baseline roles are system/user/assistant-capture/tool-capture; candidate roles add assistant-answer/tool-error. The trusted user message, top-level request settings, tools, goal contract, page URL/reading tree, and capture scope are identical. Candidate answer arguments match the archived rejected call; the following `unsupportedAnswerClaim` tool result has the same call ID. Manifest profile is context 6144, output 1024, reserve 64, so max input is 5056. This validates fixture wiring only; no model outcome is claimed.
